senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. אשר, עתר) [to be strong; denom. יֶתֶר cord, v. יִתְרָא I,] to be rich, plentiful.
to be left over.—Part. נוֹתָר m. portions of sacrifices left over beyond the legal time and bound to be burnt.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 3:4">Kerith. III, 4</cite> <he>והיה נ׳ מן וכ׳</he> and it was an overdue remnant of sacrifices.
<cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 1:1">Ib. I, 1</cite> <he>דם נ׳</he> blood of overdue sacrifices.
Meïl. I, 3, a. fr. משום נ׳ as coming under the law of nothar; a. v. fr.—Pl. נוֹתָרִים, נוֹתָרוֹת. Sifré Aḥăré Par. 5, ch. VII.—
Cant. R. to V, 14 כמה נ׳ how many laws about nothar.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 11:3">Num. R. s. 11</cite> <he>שלא לפסול … בנ׳</he> not to unfit any of the sacrifices by allowing them to become overdue.

senses.gloss: to leave over; to go beyond; to be more. Mekh. Bo s. 6 אם ה׳ if he left a part of the Passover lamb over until morning. Sifra Tsav, Par. 7, ch. XII אם ה׳ ה׳ if he has left over, he has left over (and it may be eaten). Ib. אם הוֹתִירוּ כולו if they left the whole of it over (for the second day); a. fr.—
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 34b:27">Ber. 34ᵇ</cite> <he>לא חסרתם ולא הוֹתַרְתֶּם</he> you stated the time neither too early nor too late.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 7:2">B. Bath. VII, 2</cite> <he>ה׳ כל שהוא</he> if it was somewhat more (than the stated measure).—b) <cite ref="N01392"><he>הִתִּיר</he></cite> (cmp. <cite ref="J00547"><he>הִצִּיק</he></cite> fr. <cite ref="J00547"><he>יָצַק</he></cite>), v. infra.

senses.gloss: (denom. of יָתֵר) to add; to do too much.
units: Erub. 13ᵃ שמא אתה … מְיַיתֵּר for if thou omit one letter or write one too many; Sot. 20ᵃ תַּתִּיר Hif. (v. supra).

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 27:8">Ex. R. s. 27</cite>; Tanḥ. Yithro 4 his name was Jether (Jethro) <he>שֶׁיִּ׳ פרשה וכ׳</he> because he gave rise to an additional chapter (about judges) in the Law; Mekh.

ib., Amalek, s. 1 שהוֹתִיר.—Ib. שיי׳ במעשים טובים because he did more (than ordinary men, was liberal in) good deeds. [Y. Keth. IV, end, 29ᵇ וייתר, v. יָתַר.]—Part. pass. מְיוּתָּר, pl. מְיוּתָּרִין added, superfluous.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:8:2">Koh. R. to V, 8</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="F00056"><he>ויתרון</he></cite>, <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:8:2">ib.</cite>) <he>דברים שתראה</he> (<cite ref="U00489"><he>ש</he></cite>)<he>הן מי׳ לתורה</he> (not <he>בתורה</he>) things which thou wouldst regard as additions to the Law.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:8">Ib.</cite> <he>אפי׳ דברים … מי׳ בעולם</he> even things in nature which thou wouldst believe to be superfluous (useless); <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 10">Ex. R. s. 10</cite>; (<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 10">Gen. R. s. 10</cite> <cite ref="J00740"><he>יְתֵירָה</he></cite>); a. e.
<cite ref="Yoma 46a:2">Yoma 46ᵃ</cite> <he>איברי עולה שנִתּוֹתְרוּ</he> parts of a burnt-offering which remained over (failed to be entirely burnt).
<cite ref="Pesachim 59b:7">Pes. 59ᵇ</cite> <he>כשנִיתּוֹתְרוּ</he> when they were left over (unoffered).
